Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a one-page MAP (Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a draft SOW (SOW_Redwood_v1.pdf) formatted for DocuSign. High-level summary below and next steps.

Summary of proposed MAP (6-week evaluation):
- Week 0: Kickoff & security questionnaire response (redwood to provide SOC2 artefacts)
- Week 1–2: Baseline PoC (5k tokens/day) — measure latency & cost per route
- Week 3–4: Ramp to target eval load (20k tokens/day) and enable KV prefix caching for common prompts
- Week 5: Final quality regression check + billing estimate for steady state
- Week 6: Executive review & decision window (go/no-go)

Commercial guardrails (illustrative):
- Evaluation pricing: Hosted API credits for weeks 1–2, 50% off hosted list for weeks 3–6 to cover ramp cost
- Commit trigger A (Month 1 post-eval): 100k tokens/month reserved -> 7% discount off list
- Commit trigger B (Month 3 sustained): 300k tokens/month reserved for 6-month term -> additional 6% discount (stackable)
- Renewal/expansion recommit path: If customer meets Commit B for 3 consecutive months, offer a one-time uplift credit (applied toward next quarter) and a 3–5% expansion discount depending on total committed spend

Procurement path:
- We can push the attached SOW through DocuSign once terms are agreed. For enterprise accounts we typically include an appendix for KMS/HSM and data retention.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached MAP + SOW — call out any compliance gaps
2) We align on the exact commit numbers you need for month 1 and month 3 (Rishi, Marcus — can you confirm the discount bands below?)
3) DocuSign execution target: 2027-04-28 (to meet Acme budget cycle)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through.

Kimberly Park

Kim / Marcus — quick internal note on commercial mechanics. I recommend tightening the trigger language so legal/procurement can translate to the contract easily: 

- Make Commit A a minimum monthly committed tokens metric (e.g., 100,000 tokens/month) rather than a single-month one-off. That avoids ambiguity in billing and makes the 7% discount enforceable for month-to-month invoicing.
- For Commit B, require sustained attainment (3 consecutive months at the target) before the additional 6% applies. Define "sustained" and include an explicit measurement window.
- Uplift credit: cap at a single quarter's invoice and apply as a credit line item rather than percent off to simplify accounting.
- Add failure/recovery clause: if usage drops 40% below committed baseline for 2 months, pricing reverts to standard reserved rates. We can include a grace month once per 12-month term for production on-ramps.

If Acme needs a steeper initial discount for signing DocuSign before the budget cycle, we can approve up to 10% one-time sign-on credit (subject to finance approval). Marcus — OK to leave flexibility for a one-time sign-on concession?

Rishi
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
